mechanics.scope: One dynamic convex tetrahedron with fixed isolated inclines, exposed lip and three separate fixed slot rails.
mechanics.contact_model: Proposed convex rigid-body contact; actual contact, gap and replay evidence remain required.
mechanics.material_model: Per-actor coefficients are declared in the companion Markdown card; no coefficient is calibrated or measured here.
mechanics.actuation_model: Gravity and contact determine free body motion; only declared visible latches may be prescribed.
limitations: Historical Native Bullet transfer/convergence calibration failed; this plan neither repairs nor relaxes it.
Current analytic backend cannot validate this dynamic-body scope.

route_stages.entry_intent: Release from rest toward first incline.
Unsupported path traverses open air to slot.
route_stages.mechanism: Gravity in flight, then rigid rail contact.

route_stages.exit_intent: Supported canted endpoint stays in frame.

events.physical_cause: Released tetrahedron reaches the isolated first incline.
events.measurement_required: Classify initial contact within the vertex tolerance and verify solver-derived tumble.

events.physical_cause: Tumble reaches the opposing second incline and exposed lip.
events.measurement_required: Classify a different edge contact and measure heading change; reject a hidden impulse.

events.physical_cause: Ballistic flight enters an open three-rail triangular receiver.
events.measurement_required: Measure unsupported interval, rotation range, rail contacts and sustained base support; reject snap/penetration.

camera.framing_intent: Descending camera keeps contact geometry, free-flight silhouette and slot opening in one continuous shot.

ending.description: Tetrahedron remains visibly supported in matching triangular slot.

reference_lessons.lesson: Use spatially separated supports and explicit collision geometry; no reference-media claim is made.
reference_lessons.evidence_note: This card consulted repository component/planning documentation, not a viewed reference clip; source bytes are intentionally unbound while concurrent work continues.
